push_tactic_snapshot.rationale: Continuing from ch-25 mastery; learner now applying ch-25's Q9-Q15 framework to a structurally similar domain (tool-calling data) and producing axis-extensions; application-probe-with-constructive-fix pattern emerged as additional mastery signal beyond framework-extension alone

evidence: E1 (★★): Information asymmetry by design (Q3) — Q9 spatial-axis extension. Learner critiqued APIGen-MT's Phase 2 user-simulator: because the user-LLM sees the validated blueprint (which contains ground_truth_actions), the user becomes *over-helpful* — leading or hinting at the correct tool calls — and the agent-LLM doesn't learn the reasoning step of selecting tools from a query. Framework move: extends Q9 (information anchor) into a spatial axis = *which role sees which information*. The fix (information asymmetry: hide tool list from user-LLM) is the direct architectural consequence.

E2 (★): Distribution overfitting framing (Q4) — extends Q15 into a deployment-vs-training axis. Distinct from classical overfitting (memorizing examples), distribution overfitting means the synthetic distribution silently embeds assumptions that don't hold at deployment: APIGen-MT's user-LLM-with-blueprint-visibility produces a training distribution where users are unrealistically helpful, so the trained agent performs worse on real users who don't lead. Fix proposed: real-user anchor as the only un-cheatable distribution check.

E3: BFCL field-level overfit recognition (Q7) — recognized that BFCL becoming the data spec (APIGen's four types = BFCL's first four categories; ToolACE's complexity distribution = BFCL's category distribution) is the Q4 distribution-overfit framework instantiated at the *field* level. Whoever sets the eval taxonomy sets the data-generation taxonomy. Cross-paper synthesis (APIGen + ToolACE + BFCL) reduced to one framework slot.

E4: General LLM engineering principle extracted — 'DO NOT PROVIDE THE INFORMATION UNTIL THEY NEED TO KNOW' generalized from learner's own production experience and applied as the operational rule behind information asymmetry. Promotes Q3 from chapter-specific critique to reusable engineering principle.

E5: Constructive application probe — APIGen-MT redesign. After critique, learner produced a complete architectural fix: (a) Stage 0 real corpus mining + split into Pool A (label-stripped queries) for user-LLM and Pool B (query, toolcall) pairs for agent-LLM; (b) Step 3 blueprint split into {user_part, agent_part, verifier_part}; (c) Phase 2 strict prompt isolation — user-LLM sees Pool A only, agent sees Pool B + tool schema, verifier sees ground_truth_actions post-hoc only. This is the framework-extension-as-design move from prior verdicts (ch-22 E1-E3) escalated to *constructive redesign of a published pipeline*. Probe completed within single learner turn, unprompted.

E6: ToolACE-vs-APIGen tradeoff internalization — learner correctly engaged the API-diversity-vs-execution-verification axis (Q6 sequence) and the 5-level complexity controller as a BFCL-distribution-matcher. Recognized ToolACE's tool-simulator-hallucination risk as the structural cost of broader API coverage.

E7: Blueprint-then-rollout architectural pattern absorbed (Q2 → Q4) — learner identified the blueprint-first move as separating correctness from realism, then correctly diagnosed where the separation still leaks (user-LLM blueprint visibility = E1). First understood the pattern as designed, then critiqued where it fails.

E8: Push-accepted redundancy correction — teacher flagged 'tool-name leakage from anchor split' in E5 design; learner correctly noted ('Part 2에서 user-llm한테 당연히 tool-name은 숨기고 말해야지') that this was implicit in the information-asymmetry rule and the flag was redundant. Sign of design intuition mature enough to handle the constraint without explicit teacher prompting.
rationale: Three framework extensions (E1 ★★, E2 ★, E3 cross-paper synthesis) plus a constructive application-probe redesign (E5) plus a self-extracted general engineering principle (E4) clear the bar comfortably. The Q3 information-asymmetry move is the strongest single result: it extends Q9 from an anchor-taxonomy axis into a *role-information-access* axis that applies to every multi-agent synthesis pipeline (CAMEL, AgentInstruct, K2 simulation, APIGen-MT). The constructive APIGen-MT redesign (E5) is qualitatively beyond prior chapters — learner not only critiqued but produced a complete architectural fix with concrete data-flow specification (Pool A/B split, prompt isolation rules, post-hoc verifier scope). Pattern of redundancy correction (E8) shows the design constraint was internalized at the operational level. The general engineering principle (E4) is the most reusable artifact — promoted from production experience and applied to the chapter, the principle 'do not provide information until needed' becomes available as the default tool for all future multi-agent synthesis design. Real gaps: the optional trade-off about real-corpus source (where do open-source pipelines get real user queries when production logs are inaccessible) was offered and not addressed — WildChat-class / ShareGPT / synthetic-real-style remain as candidates; learner accepted the gap and moved on. BFCL pass^k consistency metric (Q7 follow-up) was acknowledged but not engaged at the depth of Q3-Q4. ToolACE's TSS evolution operators (parameter-extension, domain-transfer, functionality-refinement) treated at chapter-text level not extension level. Net: framework-extension + constructive-redesign + reusable-principle pattern exceeds bar even within a 7-question scope. Verdict backfilled retroactively per learner request 2026-05-27.
